newsitem.title: UK: Bespak leaps after sharp rise in H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Bespak leaps after sharp rise in H1 profits.

text.p: Shares in Bespak Plc leapt on Tuesday as the maker of drug inhaling devices posted a 43 percent rise in first-half pre-tax profit coupled with an upbeat statement on new product prospects.
The stock, which rose almost 50 percent during 1996, was up 44p at 525 by 1255 GMT in thin volume of 10,000 shares.
Bespak said pre-tax profit rose to 5.0 million stg in the six months ended November 1 from 3.5 million stg a year before, on turnover up 10 percent to 39.4 million stg.
Earnings per share rose 45 percent to 13.3p and the dividend was raised 10 percent to 4.62p.
Operating margins grew to 12.8 percent from 10.2 percent.
Bespak chairman Sir David Cooksey said the company's first- half results were boosted by strong demand for asthma inhaler valves and growth in new products.

"The board believes that Bespak has substantial opportunities for long-term growth," Cooksey said. "The progress in the last six months and the strengthening of the organisation increases the group's ability to take full advantage of those opportunities."
"During the second half year continued progress is expected versus last year in the UK, resulting primarily from further growth in sales of drug delivery devices."
Bespak also said it appointed Roger Mann, group finance director of engineering group Siebe Plc, as a non-executive director.
